quality_check.description: A vertical 9:16 cave-framed gallery scene centers the recurring glass orb in the foreground. The orb retains its spherical form, aged-bronze equatorial band, moss-green cord knot, clawed cradle and large crescent brace. Long crone-like fingers cradle the orb beside a ragged moss-green garment, while a separate elongated hand hangs between a nude classical statue and a curtained changing booth. Within the orb are reflected miniature glimpses of the statue, changing booth and two exposed figures on a beach-like ground. The surrounding scene uses warm limestone, ochre, sienna, umber and charcoal tones with rough stone texture and hand-drawn mineral-fresco linework.

The requested restrained side-eye cue from the crone is absent because her face is almost entirely concealed.

EPISODE TOPIC: Why Are Humans Ashamed of Being Naked?
EPISODE DIRECTION: Slow push-in through a quiet sculpture-gallery alcove: a nude marble figure stands openly beside a fabric changing booth, its privacy curtain still taut from being snapped shut. The crone’s long finger hangs precisely between exposed stone body and concealed living body, her restrained side-eye catching the contradiction. From beneath the same ragged moss-green sleeve, her other long fingers deliberately cradle a luminous orb, whose surface reflects matched glimpses of gallery nudity, private changing, and ordinary beach exposure.
